scope: Real local LLM planning, canonical scene-contract assembly, schema checks and final H3 prompt compilation on synthetic fixtures. No video or audio is generated by these evaluations. Automatic passes are not visual-quality scores.

hardware: Single NVIDIA RTX 4090 with 24 GB VRAM; sequential exclusive model ownership.
methodology: Historical scores remain unchanged. Scene check versions differ: v1 rejected all extra prop rows; v2 permits exact authored workbench/stool; v3 also permits exact authored empty doorway. Unknown props, token aliases and duplicate authored instances remain failures.
Canonical assembly can repair omitted or incorrect raw director rows. Success therefore measures the current production pipeline, not model-only scene understanding.
One completed schema-valid semantic stage may be repaired when enabled. Uncertain transport and incomplete token-truncated output are not retried by that policy.

Effective output tokens per second sums API-reported completion_tokens across stages with usage, including a truncated response when present, divided by their measured whole-stage wall time. It includes prompt processing, transport and validation, not pure decode rate. It is not successful-turn throughput.
Stochastic sampling, changing code/checks, warm caches and simultaneous CPU work prevent controlled causal comparisons of timing or pass fractions.

The exact replay reuses two labelled saved stages and makes one fresh director call with identical system/content/schema. Fresh answer length may differ; success does not prove that every similar request needs or fits its new allowance.
